title: Two high-speed trains collide near Los Yébenes, Toledo; Spanish media report dozens dead
dek: A Renfe AVE and an Iryo train collided on the Madrid-Andalusia line on the morning of 28 October. The death toll is still being reported and the cause is not established.
what: Spanish outlets report that a Renfe AVE train and an Iryo train collided at about 8:54 a.m. local time on Wednesday 28 October 2026 near Los Yébenes, in Toledo province, on the Madrid-Seville high-speed line. El Diario de Madrid reports that two carriages fell down an embankment, and quotes Adif, the rail infrastructure operator, saying the Madrid-Andalusia high-speed line was interrupted by a collision between two trains. Iryo said it had activated its emergency protocols and suspended its services.

The count of the dead has moved. OKDiario's live page, updated at 12:07 Central European time, lists Protección Civil giving "at least 46" dead at 10:42 and 50 at 11:13, and a Castilla-La Mancha regional government spokesperson saying 30 at 11:53, with the figure expected to rise. It also cites union sources saying at least 39. I could not find an official final count, and I read these pages through a fetch tool that summarises them, so the figures are as that live page reported them. They may already be out of date.

The cause is not established. OKDiario says the government first pointed to human error and that later reporting pointed to a signalling safety system. Both are reported claims, and I found no official finding. One post on X says a Renfe train ran a red signal; that is a claim in a post and is not used as fact here.
why: Rail disasters with a large death toll draw fast attention, and the first hours carry conflicting numbers and causes. The posts that spread first gave a toll that official bodies were still revising.
next: An official casualty count from Spanish authorities, and the findings of the rail accident investigators on cause.
